reviews.summary: A major Binance security incident on October 29 involved 233.46M XRP sent from hot wallets to attacker-controlled addresses. Binance says remediation is ongoing, creating near-term XRP-specific custody, liquidity, and headline-risk uncertainty.
materialRisks: Binance reports that 233.46M XRP was transferred from five hot wallets to attacker-controlled addresses during its October 29 security incident; the investigation and asset-tracing process remain ongoing. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/384328127385979?utm_source=openai))

The incident affected approximately US$6.34B across assets; Binance says it replenished 98% of affected tokens and has frozen/intercepted about US$2.85B, but reconciliation and recovery remain incomplete. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/en/square/post/384328127385979?utm_source=openai))

facts.fact: Binance’s official update, published November 3, states that the XRP transfers occurred between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC on October 29, 2026. ([binance.com](https://www.binance.com/fr-AF/blog/community/3229153443759566763?utm_source=openai))

XRPL’s public status page reported its services operational on November 4, with no November incidents reported; this does not remove the exchange/custody risk above. ([status.ai.xrpl.org](https://status.ai.xrpl.org/incidents?utm_source=openai))
The market venue for XRP-EUR was not supplied, so no venue-specific maintenance, order-cancellation, or withdrawal restriction was attributed to this signal.
